license: Public domain in the US: Commons tag {{PD-US}} (19th-century published engraving). Original held by Chicago History Museum.
credit_line: Raising the Briggs House, Chicago (engraving, c. 1866). Chicago History Museum / Wikimedia Commons, public domain
what_it_shows: HERO SHOT. The Briggs House hotel ('BRIGGS HOUSE' lettered across the facade) sitting on timber cribbing at street corner; a long line of workmen crouched along both walls turning jackscrews; three foremen stand on a platform at the corner; crowds watch from the street; people on the hotel balconies and in upper windows.
date_note: DATE DISPUTED: Commons says '1857 or 1866'. Primary sources (Chicago Tribune 7 Feb 1866 and 10 Nov 1866) show the Briggs House was raised in 1866, so 1866 is most likely. It is the Briggs House, NOT the Tremont House: do not caption it as the Tremont.
best_segments: Hook / 'how' sentence. Slow push from full frame into the row of men at the screws (approx x 500-1300, y 650-950 of 2072x1150). Vertical 9:16 crop: centre on the corner (x 700-1350). Balcony crowd (x 1200-1880, y 330-450) works for 'guests stayed inside'.

license: Public domain in the US: Commons tag {{PD-US}} (published 19th-century lithograph). Original in Chicago History Museum.
credit_line: Edward Mendel (lithographer), raising of the Lake Street block, Chicago (1860). Chicago History Museum / Wikimedia Commons, public domain
what_it_shows: The whole north side of Lake Street between LaSalle and Clark: Marine Bank (left) and a continuous row of 4-5 storey brick stores, lifted onto timber cribbing several feet above the street; the sidewalk is hung from the block and shoppers walk along it; workmen and jacks visible in the gap at the base; carriages and crowds in the foreground.
date_note: DATE DISPUTED: Commons says 1857 and the Encyclopedia of Chicago captions it 1855, but the Chicago Press and Tribune (12 May 1860) says the three contracting firms commissioned this Mendel lithograph of the 1860 Lake Street raising; the stores and Marine Bank match the 1860 job. Use '1860'.
best_segments: Wide establishing pan left-to-right along the raised row (Ken Burns). Detail: base of the block with cribbing and workers (y 680-760 of 1352). Good for 'a city lifting itself' and the 600 men / 6,000 screws block.

credit_line: 'Raising a Block of Buildings in Chicago', John W. Barber & Henry Howe, The Loyal West in the Times of the Rebellion (1865), p. 764. Public domain
what_it_shows: Street-level view of the Lake Street block mid-raise: corner building 'Culver Page & Hoyne' on cribbing, timber piles and screws along the base, ramps to the sidewalk, carts in the street. Printed caption: 320-foot front raised 'four feet and two thirds, by 6,000 screws ... turned, at signals, by a force of 600 men', five days.
best_segments: Low-res (612 px): use small in frame or as a quick insert; the caption text is a ready-made on-screen citation for '600 men / 6,000 screws'. Crop out caption for picture-only (y 0-530).

what_it_shows: Real photograph of the Tremont House (the hotel raised six feet in 1861): six-storey brick hotel with cupola at the corner of Lake and Dearborn, unpaved street, barrels on the sidewalk. Stereo card, two near-identical frames on yellow mount.
best_segments: Crop LEFT frame only (approx x 400-2880, y 170-2680) for the 'Tremont House' name-reveal or twist; vertical crop on the hotel corner (x 400-1900). Not the raising itself; it shows the hotel after it was raised.

best_segments: 'Before' shot for the hotel; crop out the page border/masthead (x 200-1420, y 140-870). Grainy; use briefly.

best_segments: Best-looking Tremont image for the hook/name card. Crop the hotel (x 150-2050, y 650-2450 of 3600x2861); slow push toward the front steps/entrance for the 'steps got steeper' twist.
